questions.question_text:
In the following ARM template snippet, which resource group is being created?
```json
{
  "type": "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups",
  "apiVersion": "2021-04-01",
  "name": "rg-prod",
  "location": "EastUS"
}
```
questions.explanation: The "name" property defines the resource group name. In the snippet it is "rg-prod", so option A is correct.

questions.question_text: Which section of an ARM template is used to declare parameters that can be supplied during deployment?
questions.explanation: The "parameters" section defines input parameters that users can provide values for when deploying the template. It is not the resources, variables, or metadata sections.

questions.question_text: You need to add a new property to the virtual machine resource in an existing Bicep file. Which part of the file should you edit?
questions.explanation: The "resources" block contains the definitions of the Azure resources. To modify a VM, you edit the VM resource definition inside the resources block.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command correctly deploys a Bicep file named deploy.bicep to a resource group?
questions.explanation: The Azure CLI command `az deployment group create` with the `--template-file` argument is used to deploy a Bicep (or ARM JSON) template to a specified resource group.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a valid method to export an ARM template from the Azure portal?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the "Export template" button on the resource group

options.label: C
options.text: Use Azure CLI az deployment group export

options.label: D
options.text: Use the "Download" option on a resource in the portal

questions.explanation: Azure CLI does not provide a direct `az deployment group export` command for exporting templates. Export is performed via the portal's Export template button, PowerShell cmdlet, or manual download of the JSON.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the "dependsOn" property in an ARM template?

options.label: C
options.text: Sets the location of the resource

questions.explanation: "dependsOn" tells Azure Resource Manager the order in which resources should be deployed, ensuring that a resource is created only after its dependencies are available.

questions.question_text: Which statement about using modules in a Bicep file is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Modules cannot be reused across multiple templates

options.label: B
options.text: The module path must be an absolute file system path

options.label: C
options.text: Parameters can be passed to a module

options.label: D
options.text: Outputs of a module are not accessible to the parent template

questions.explanation: Bicep modules accept parameters, allowing them to be reused with different inputs. The path can be relative, and module outputs are available to the calling template.

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command exports an existing resource group as an ARM template to a local file?

options.label: B
options.text: az deployment group create --template-file rg1.json --resource-group RG1

questions.explanation: The `az group export` command creates an ARM template representing the specified resource group and writes it to the given file path.

questions.question_text: In an Azure DevOps pipeline, which task should you use to deploy an ARM template?
questions.explanation: The Azure Resource Manager deployment task in Azure DevOps is specifically designed to deploy ARM templates (including Bicep) to Azure.

questions.question_text: A Bicep file defines a parameter named location with a default value of "eastus". If you run the deployment without specifying a location, what happens?

options.label: A
options.text: Deployment fails because location is mandatory

options.label: C
options.text: Location is automatically set to the resource group's location

options.label: D
options.text: Location defaults to "westus" regardless of the template

questions.explanation: When a parameter has a default value and the user does not provide a value during deployment, the default is applied. Hence, "eastus" will be used.
